note: NORMAL data only; false-alarm transfer. Recall on real attacks needs a fresh registered split.

methods_legend.S0_fit_sigma: pooled top-3 |residual|/sigma, sigma from the FIT period (rt2-style)
methods_legend.S1_calib_sigma: pooled, sigma from the CALIBRATION period
methods_legend.S2_calib_mad: pooled, robust MAD scale from calibration
methods_legend.S3_per_var_union: per-variable union, each variable Bonferroni-calibrated to target/d
methods_legend.S4_margin2x: S2 but calibrated to half the budget (conservative safety margin)
methods_legend.S5_daily_recal: daily re-calibration of the threshold on the previous day (online)

findings: Calibration transfer for the world-model residual detector on HAI normal data is a MILD drift: pooled residual scores overshoot the false-alarm budget by at most ~1.16x on the drifty release (23.05) and stay under budget on the others. This is not the catastrophe the rt2 D2/D2c numbers (108-134 false alarms/day) implied -- that was the incident-trained classifier's score distribution failing, a different and worse problem than the world-model residual.

The adopted better forecaster (gbr_big_h12) slightly IMPROVES calibration transfer too: worst-case overshoot fell from ~1.35x with the baseline ridge+GBR(history 3) to ~1.16x with h12. Tighter, more stationary residuals transfer better. The two improvements compound.

A conservative safety margin (S4: calibrate the threshold to half the budget) keeps the deploy false-positive rate UNDER budget on all three releases (worst 0.60x). This is the robust, data-free fix for what failed in rt2. Cost: a stricter threshold reduces sensitivity, so the attack-recall impact must be measured on a fresh registered split before this is a detection claim.

Naive per-variable union (S3) is catastrophic (up to x34 on the low-drift release): a single narrowly-distributed sensor's tiny deploy shift blows past its tight per-variable threshold and the union fires constantly. Do not multi-test per variable without far more conservative calibration.

Daily re-calibration (S5) tracks the target well (geomean ~1.06) but still mildly overshoots on the drifty release and assumes recent normal data is observable (an attack in the trailing window would relax the threshold).
recommendation: Use gbr_big_h12 residuals with a pooled robust (MAD) score (S2) and a conservative safety margin (S4, calibrate to ~half the budget). Avoid per-variable union. If online benign data is available, daily re-calibration (S5) is an alternative.
